// The scaffold's first test: the DI tree composes and every language is
// registered. Deliberately grammar-agnostic, so it keeps passing once you
// replace the starter grammar with your own.
//
// `createServices()` not throwing is itself an assertion — the framework's
// `assertCoreSlotsBound` runs during bootstrap and fails loudly when a module
// is missing from the composition.

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createServices } from '../src/node/services.js';

describe('Bookstore services', () => {
   it('composes the DI tree and registers exactly one language', () => {
      const { shared } = createServices();

      const registered = shared.ServiceRegistry.all.map(language => language.LanguageMetaData);
      expect(registered.map(metadata => metadata.languageId)).toEqual(['bookstore']);
      expect(registered.flatMap(metadata => [...metadata.fileExtensions])).toEqual(['.bookstore']);
   });

   it('binds a reflection covering the generated AST', () => {
      const { shared } = createServices();

      expect(shared.AstReflection.getAllTypes().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
   });
});

==============================================================================
server/test/parsing.test.ts
==============================================================================
// Tier one of the three a new language breaks in order: does my rule parse.
//
// Grammar-derived, so replacing the starter grammar replaces this file — but
// the SHAPE survives, which is the point of scaffolding it: the questions stay
// the same for every language, only the source text changes.

import { parseHelper } from '@hydranium/core/testing';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { BookstoreModel } from '../src/language-server/ast.js';
import { createServices } from '../src/node/services.js';

describe('Bookstore parsing', () => {
   it('parses the starter rules and populates the AST', async () => {
      const { Bookstore } = createServices();

      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)('node first -> second\nnode second', {
         documentUri: 'file:///parsing.bookstore'
      });

      expect(document.parseResult.lexerErrors).toHaveLength(0);
      expect(document.parseResult.parserErrors).toHaveLength(0);
      expect(document.parseResult.value.nodes.map(node => node.name)).toEqual(['first', 'second']);
   });

   it('reports a parser error for text the grammar does not accept', async () => {
      const { Bookstore } = createServices();

      // The name is mandatory, so this is a parse failure rather than a
      // validation one — nothing downstream of the parser runs on it.
      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)('node -> second', {
         documentUri: 'file:///invalid.bookstore'
      });

      expect(document.parseResult.parserErrors.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
   });
});

==============================================================================
server/test/linking.test.ts
==============================================================================
// Tier two: does my cross-reference resolve.
//
// Both cases matter and they fail for different reasons. A same-document
// reference resolves through local scope alone; a cross-document one needs the
// declaring document's exports in the shared global index, which is what a
// multi-file workspace depends on and what a single-document test cannot see.

import { parseHelper } from '@hydranium/core/testing';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { AstUtils } from '@hydranium/langium';
import type { BookstoreModel } from '../src/language-server/ast.js';
import { createServices } from '../src/node/services.js';

describe('Bookstore linking', () => {
   it('resolves a reference within one document', async () => {
      const { shared, Bookstore } = createServices();

      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)('node first -> second\nnode second', {
         documentUri: 'file:///within.bookstore'
      });
      await shared.workspace.DocumentBuilder.build([document]);

      expect(document.parseResult.value.nodes[0].target?.ref?.name).toBe('second');
   });

   it('resolves a reference across documents, through the shared index', async () => {
      const { shared, Bookstore } = createServices();
      const parse = parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore);

      const declaring = await parse('node second', { documentUri: 'file:///declaring.bookstore' });
      const referencing = await parse('node first -> second', { documentUri: 'file:///referencing.bookstore' });
      await shared.workspace.DocumentBuilder.build([declaring, referencing]);

      // The URI, not just the name: the referencing document declares no
      // `second` of its own, but asserting WHERE the target came from is what
      // keeps this about the global index rather than about local scope.
      const target = referencing.parseResult.value.nodes[0].target?.ref;
      expect(target?.name).toBe('second');
      expect(target ? AstUtils.getDocument(target).uri.toString() : undefined).toBe('file:///declaring.bookstore');
   });
});

==============================================================================
server/test/validating.test.ts
==============================================================================
// Tier three: does a broken model get reported.
//
// A dangling reference is the FRAMEWORK's own linker diagnostic; a repeated
// name is reported by the scaffold's own validation check. Bind a further
// check in your language module and assert it here alongside these.

import { parseHelper } from '@hydranium/core/testing';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { DiagnosticSeverity } from 'vscode-languageserver';
import type { BookstoreModel } from '../src/language-server/ast.js';
import { createServices } from '../src/node/services.js';

describe('Bookstore validation', () => {
   it('reports nothing for a well-formed document', async () => {
      const { shared, Bookstore } = createServices();

      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)('node first -> second\nnode second', {
         documentUri: 'file:///valid.bookstore'
      });
      await shared.workspace.DocumentBuilder.build([document], { validation: true });

      expect(document.diagnostics ?? []).toHaveLength(0);
   });

   it('reports an error for a reference that resolves to nothing', async () => {
      const { shared, Bookstore } = createServices();

      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)('node first -> absent', {
         documentUri: 'file:///dangling.bookstore'
      });
      await shared.workspace.DocumentBuilder.build([document], { validation: true });

      const diagnostics = document.diagnostics ?? [];
      expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(diagnostics[0].severity).toBe(DiagnosticSeverity.Error);
      expect(diagnostics[0].message).toContain('absent');
   });

   it('warns on each node named like one before it', async () => {
      const { shared, Bookstore } = createServices();

      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)('node first\nnode second\nnode first', {
         documentUri: 'file:///duplicate.bookstore'
      });
      await shared.workspace.DocumentBuilder.build([document], { validation: true });

      const diagnostics = document.diagnostics ?? [];
      expect(diagnostics).toHaveLength(1);
      expect(diagnostics[0].severity).toBe(DiagnosticSeverity.Warning);
      expect(diagnostics[0].message).toBe("A node named 'first' is already declared.");
      expect(diagnostics[0].range.start.line).toBe(2);
   });
});

==============================================================================
server/test/serialization.test.ts
==============================================================================
// Round-trips each grammar through its serializer: parse the source, serialize
// the model, compare the text. The serializer is the parser's inverse, so this
// is the assertion that keeps a client session's `update` / `save` writing
// files the language server can read back.
//
// The transfer case is the one that catches the mistake worth catching.
// `ModelService.modelToText` short-circuits only a RAW STRING, so a typed model
// from the data head reaches `serializeTransfer` — where a cross-reference is a
// plain string, not a `Reference`.

import { parseHelper } from '@hydranium/core/testing';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import type { BookstoreModel } from '../src/language-server/ast.js';
import { BookstoreModel as TransferBookstoreModel, BookstoreNode } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { createServices } from '../src/node/services.js';
import { transferNode } from './generated-hydranium/transfer-builder.js';

describe('Bookstore serialization', () => {
   const source = 'node first -> second\nnode second';

   it('round-trips parsed source back to the same text', async () => {
      const { Bookstore } = createServices();

      const document = await parseHelper<BookstoreModel>(Bookstore)(source, { documentUri: 'file:///round-trip.bookstore' });

      expect(document.parseResult.parserErrors).toHaveLength(0);
      expect(await Bookstore.serializer.Serializer.serializeAst(document.parseResult.value)).toBe(source);
   });

   it('emits the same text from a transfer model, whose references are plain strings', async () => {
      const { Bookstore } = createServices();
      const model = transferNode(TransferBookstoreModel, {
         nodes: [transferNode(BookstoreNode, { name: 'first', target: 'second' }), transferNode(BookstoreNode, { name: 'second' })]
      });

      expect(await Bookstore.serializer.Serializer.serializeTransfer(model)).toBe(source);
   });
});

client/README.md

# bookstore-client

The host-neutral client side of the Bookstore language: what every host of it
mounts, whatever that host is. It reads the element ids from the protocol
package and never depends on the server.

- `src/bookstore-diagram-module.ts` — the `Bookstore` diagram: a registration per element type, its container module, and `initializeBookstoreDiagramContainer`
- `src/index.ts` — the package root, re-exporting each module

A host builds a diagram container with the initializer, passing its own
modules: they go first and the diagram definition last, since GLSP gives an
element type to whichever module registered it last.

==============================================================================
client/src/index.ts
==============================================================================
// What every host of the Bookstore language mounts.

export * from './bookstore-diagram-module.js';

==============================================================================
client/src/bookstore-diagram-module.ts
==============================================================================
// The client side of the Bookstore diagram: how each element type the server
// stamps is drawn. It binds nothing a host owns, so every host mounts this one
// module and adds its own beside it.

import {
   angleOfPoint,
   configureModelElement,
   type ContainerConfiguration,
   type GEdge,
   GEdgeView,
   GNode,
   initializeDiagramContainer,
   Point,
   type RenderingContext,
   RoundedCornerNodeView,
   svg,
   toDegrees
} from '@eclipse-glsp/client';
import { configureHydraniumModelElements, HydraniumGEdge } from '@hydranium/glsp-client';
import { type Container, ContainerModule, injectable } from 'inversify';
import {
   BOOKSTORE_EDGE_TYPE,
   BOOKSTORE_EXTERNAL_NODE_TYPE,
   BOOKSTORE_NODE_TYPE,
   type BookstoreElementType
} from 'bookstore-protocol';

/** GLSP's edge view plus an arrowhead at the target, so an edge reads in the direction of its reference. */
@injectable()
export class BookstoreEdgeView extends GEdgeView {
   protected override renderAdditionals(edge: GEdge, segments: Point[], context: RenderingContext) {
      const end = segments[segments.length - 1];
      const degrees = toDegrees(angleOfPoint(Point.subtract(segments[segments.length - 2], end)));
      const arrow = svg('path', {
         'class-sprotty-edge-arrow': true,
         d: 'M 0,0 L 10,-4 L 10,4 Z',
         transform: `rotate(${degrees} ${end.x} ${end.y}) translate(${end.x} ${end.y})`
      });
      return [...super.renderAdditionals(edge, segments, context), arrow];
   }
}

/** The model class and view one element type renders through, as `configureModelElement` takes them. */
export interface BookstoreElementRegistration {
   readonly model: Parameters<typeof configureModelElement>[2];
   readonly view: Parameters<typeof configureModelElement>[3];
}

/**
 * One registration per element type the server stamps.
 *
 * Keyed by the protocol's union of ids, so an id added there does not compile
 * until it is drawn here: sprotty renders a type with no registration as
 * nothing, with only a console warning.
 */
export const BOOKSTORE_ELEMENT_REGISTRATIONS: Readonly<Record<BookstoreElementType, BookstoreElementRegistration>> = {
   [BOOKSTORE_NODE_TYPE]: { model: GNode, view: RoundedCornerNodeView },
   // Drawn like a node of the document; the server marks it with the `external` CSS class.
   [BOOKSTORE_EXTERNAL_NODE_TYPE]: { model: GNode, view: RoundedCornerNodeView },
   // The framework's edge rather than `GEdge`: GLSP's gives the labels of an
   // edge without bendpoints no finite bounds, and fitting the diagram to its
   // pane then blanks the canvas.
   [BOOKSTORE_EDGE_TYPE]: { model: HydraniumGEdge, view: BookstoreEdgeView }
};

/** GLSP's default model elements, plus the registrations above. */
export const bookstoreDiagramModule = new ContainerModule((bind, unbind, isBound, rebind) => {
   const context = { bind, unbind, isBound, rebind };
   configureHydraniumModelElements(context);
   for (const [elementTypeId, registration] of Object.entries(BOOKSTORE_ELEMENT_REGISTRATIONS)) {
      configureModelElement(context, elementTypeId, registration.model, registration.view);
   }
});

/**
 * Build a Bookstore diagram container: the host's modules first and this
 * diagram's definition last, since GLSP gives an element type to whichever
 * module registered it last.
 */
export function initializeBookstoreDiagramContainer(container: Container, ...modules: ContainerConfiguration) {
   return initializeDiagramContainer(container, ...modules, bookstoreDiagramModule);
}

vscode-servers/README.md
==============================================================================
# bookstore-vscode-servers

A VS Code extension that starts the Bookstore server and contributes no editor,
view or command: the languages, their grammars and the server. With a socket
head, it also answers each head’s port under a host command, which a host
without a language client of its own runs: the Theia applications in
`../host-theia-browser` and `../host-theia-electron`, which sideload this
extension. The VS Code extension in `../host-vscode` starts the server through
the same function. Both work side by side, but each starts its own server and
language client, so diagnostics may show twice: install one.

```bash
npm run build   # copy the server’s grammars and compile into out/; build the server first
npm run watch   # the same on every change
```

- `src/extension.ts` — activation, which starts the server and, with a socket head, registers its port commands
- `src/language-client.ts` — the server launch, shared with `../host-vscode`

==============================================================================

==============================================================================
// The extension, compiled to CommonJS in `out/`, which the extension host
// loads. It runs in Node, so it has no DOM. The declarations are for the VS
// Code extension, which imports the launch from `out/`.

    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "rootDir": "src",
    "outDir": "out",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "sourceMap": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "types": ["node"]

vscode-servers/src/extension.ts
==============================================================================
// The servers-only extension: it starts the Bookstore server and contributes no
// editor, view or command. A Theia app sideloads this one rather than the VS
// Code extension, whose diagram editors would give its files a second editor.

import { registerPortCommands } from '@hydranium/client-vscode/node';
import {
   BOOKSTORE_DATA_SERVER_HOST_COMMAND,
   BOOKSTORE_DATA_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND,
   BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_HOST_COMMAND,
   BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND
} from 'bookstore-protocol';
import type { ExtensionContext } from 'vscode';
import type { LanguageClient } from 'vscode-languageclient/node';
import { startBookstoreLanguageClient } from './language-client.js';

let client: LanguageClient | undefined;

export async function activate(context: ExtensionContext): Promise<void> {
   client = await startBookstoreLanguageClient(context);

   // Each socket head's port as a host command, for a host with no language
   // client of its own. Not in the shared launch: VS Code throws on a second
   // registration of one id, so the VS Code extension beside this one would fail
   // to activate. A pass-through: awaiting anything else in it would hang a
   // Theia backend on a user dismissing a notification.
   registerPortCommands(context, client, {
      [BOOKSTORE_DATA_SERVER_HOST_COMMAND]: BOOKSTORE_DATA_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND,
      [BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_HOST_COMMAND]: BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND
   });
}

export async function deactivate(): Promise<void> {
   await client?.stop();
   client = undefined;
}

==============================================================================
vscode-servers/src/language-client.ts
==============================================================================
// Starts the Bookstore server for VS Code, and for a Theia app that sideloads
// this extension: one launch, so both hand the server the same documents.

import { ALL_LANGUAGES } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { type ExtensionContext, workspace } from 'vscode';
import { LanguageClient, TransportKind } from 'vscode-languageclient/node';

/** Fork the server, start its language client and return it once started. */
export async function startBookstoreLanguageClient(context: ExtensionContext): Promise<LanguageClient> {
   // Resolved through the package, so it works from the workspace and from an
   // installed extension alike. Over IPC, which keeps the server's stdout free.
   const serverModule = require.resolve('bookstore-server/lib/main.js');
   const extensions = ALL_LANGUAGES.flatMap(language => language.fileExtensions).join(',');
   const client = new LanguageClient(
      'bookstore',
      'Bookstore',
      { module: serverModule, transport: TransportKind.ipc },
      {
         documentSelector: ALL_LANGUAGES.map(({ languageId }) => ({ scheme: 'file', language: languageId })),
         // Changes on disk the editor does not hold, such as a file another tool writes.
         synchronize: { fileEvents: workspace.createFileSystemWatcher(`**/*{${extensions}}`) }
      }
   );
   context.subscriptions.push(client);
   await client.start();

   return client;
}

theia/README.md
==============================================================================
# bookstore-theia

The Bookstore Theia extension: reconnect hardening, a Show Model command reading
a file through the data head, and a diagram editor for each diagram. The
language client is not here: the application sideloads `../vscode-servers`,
which starts the server and answers each socket head’s port under a host
command, and the backend modules forward the page’s channels to those ports. The
applications in `../host-theia-browser` and `../host-theia-electron` run it.

```bash
npm run build   # compile into lib/; build the protocol and client packages first
```

## Layout

- `src/browser/bookstore-connection-preload-module.ts` and `src/node/bookstore-connection-backend-module.ts` — reconnect hardening, sized by the application’s `connectionBufferBytes`
- `src/browser/bookstore-frontend-module.ts` — the frontend bindings
- `src/browser/bookstore-data-port.ts` and `bookstore-data-connection.ts` — the data head’s connection
- `src/browser/bookstore-show-model-command.ts` — `Bookstore: Show Model`, reading the current file through the data head
- `src/node/bookstore-data-backend-module.ts` — forwards the data channel to the data head’s port
- `src/common/bookstore-glsp-contribution.ts` — the id the GLSP client and its forwarder share
- `src/browser/bookstore-glsp-client-contribution.ts` — the GLSP client every diagram shares
- `src/node/bookstore-glsp-backend-module.ts` — forwards the GLSP channel to the GLSP head’s port
- `src/browser/bookstore-diagram-frontend-module.ts` — the `Bookstore` diagram editor, over the client package’s diagram
- `style/diagram.css` — the diagrams’ colours, from the Theia theme

// The extension, compiled to CommonJS in `lib/`, which the Theia application
// bundles: `src/browser/` into the page, `src/node/` into the backend. The

// bundler, so tsc does not resolve it.

    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM"],
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "rootDir": "src",
    "outDir": "lib",
    "strict": true,
    "strictPropertyInitialization": false,
    "experimentalDecorators": true,
    "emitDecoratorMetadata": true,
    "noUncheckedSideEffectImports": false,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "sourceMap": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "types": ["node"]
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}

==============================================================================
theia/src/browser/bookstore-connection-preload-module.ts
==============================================================================
// The reconnect hardening, browser side: messages sent while the socket is
// down are buffered and replayed, rather than the page reloading.
//
// A `frontendPreload` entry, not a `frontend` one: Theia builds its connection
// before any frontend module runs, so a rebind there would do nothing. The
// buffer size is the application's `theia.frontend.config.connectionBufferBytes`.

import { bindConnectionResilience } from '@hydranium/client-theia/browser';
import { FrontendApplicationConfigProvider } from '@theia/core/lib/browser/frontend-application-config-provider';
import { ContainerModule } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';

export default new ContainerModule((_bind, _unbind, isBound, rebind) => {
   const bufferBytes = FrontendApplicationConfigProvider.get()['connectionBufferBytes'];
   bindConnectionResilience(isBound, rebind, { bufferBytes: typeof bufferBytes === 'number' ? bufferBytes : undefined });
});

==============================================================================
theia/src/browser/bookstore-frontend-module.ts
==============================================================================
// The Bookstore Theia extension's frontend: the connection’s lifecycle in an
// Output channel, a warning when an outage outlasts the offline buffer, editor
// disk sync, the data head’s connection and the Show Model command, and the
// GLSP client the diagrams share.

import { GLSPClientContribution } from '@eclipse-glsp/theia-integration';
import { bindChannelLogger, bindConnectionDiagnostics, bindEditorDiskSync } from '@hydranium/client-theia/browser';
import { bindDataConnection } from '@hydranium/data-client-theia/browser';
import { CommandContribution } from '@theia/core';
import { ContainerModule } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';
import { BookstoreDataConnection } from './bookstore-data-connection.js';
import { BookstoreDataPort } from './bookstore-data-port.js';
import { BookstoreGlspClientContribution } from './bookstore-glsp-client-contribution.js';
import { BookstoreShowModelCommand } from './bookstore-show-model-command.js';

export default new ContainerModule((bind, _unbind, isBound, rebind) => {
   bindChannelLogger(bind, { channelName: 'Bookstore Connection' });
   bindConnectionDiagnostics(bind);
   // Keeps an editor from writing over a file a head saved while it held the same text unsaved.
   bindEditorDiskSync(bind, isBound, rebind);

   // The data head: one connection, opened when the command first runs.
   bind(BookstoreDataPort).toSelf().inSingletonScope();
   bindDataConnection(bind, isBound, BookstoreDataConnection);
   bind(BookstoreShowModelCommand).toSelf().inSingletonScope();
   bind(CommandContribution).toService(BookstoreShowModelCommand);

   // One GLSP client for every diagram, so each diagram module skips binding its own.
   bind(BookstoreGlspClientContribution).toSelf().inSingletonScope();
   bind(GLSPClientContribution).toService(BookstoreGlspClientContribution);
});

theia/src/node/bookstore-connection-backend-module.ts
==============================================================================
// The reconnect hardening, backend side: the session outlives a dropped socket
// for the application's `frontendConnectionTimeout`, and messages for the page
// wait in a buffer of `theia.backend.config.connectionBufferBytes`.

import { bindConnectionResilience } from '@hydranium/client-theia/node';
import { BackendApplicationConfigProvider } from '@theia/core/lib/node/backend-application-config-provider';
import { ContainerModule } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';

export default new ContainerModule((bind, _unbind, isBound, rebind) => {
   const bufferBytes = BackendApplicationConfigProvider.get()['connectionBufferBytes'];
   bindConnectionResilience(bind, isBound, rebind, { bufferBytes: typeof bufferBytes === 'number' ? bufferBytes : undefined });
});

import { injectable } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';

@injectable()
export class BookstoreDataPort extends ChannelDataPort {
   protected readonly servicePath = DATA_SERVER_PATH;

theia/src/browser/bookstore-data-connection.ts
==============================================================================
// The page's one connection to the data head. Everything that reads the data
// head takes a session off it: Theia opens one channel per service path.

import { DataConnectionWithEvents } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import { inject, injectable } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';
import type { BookstoreElement } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { BookstoreDataPort } from './bookstore-data-port.js';

@injectable()
export class BookstoreDataConnection extends DataConnectionWithEvents<BookstoreElement> {
   // The constructor, not a field: the port is needed before `super` returns.
   constructor(@inject(BookstoreDataPort) port: BookstoreDataPort) {
      super(port);
   }
}

==============================================================================
theia/src/browser/bookstore-show-model-command.ts
==============================================================================
// `Bookstore: Show Model`: the current editor's file, text or diagram, read
// through the data head, and its root type shown in a notification.

import { Command, type CommandContribution, type CommandRegistry, MessageService, nls } from '@theia/core';
import { ApplicationShell, NavigatableWidget } from '@theia/core/lib/browser';
import { inject, injectable } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';
import { ALL_LANGUAGES } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { BookstoreDataConnection } from './bookstore-data-connection.js';

export const SHOW_MODEL_COMMAND = Command.toLocalizedCommand(
   { id: 'bookstore.showModel', label: 'Show Model', category: 'Bookstore' },
   'bookstore/showModel',
   'bookstore/category'
);

@injectable()
export class BookstoreShowModelCommand implements CommandContribution {
   @inject(BookstoreDataConnection) protected readonly connection: BookstoreDataConnection;
   @inject(ApplicationShell) protected readonly shell: ApplicationShell;
   @inject(MessageService) protected readonly messages: MessageService;

   // Opened on the first run and kept: the connection ends it with the page.
   protected session?: ReturnType<BookstoreDataConnection['createSession']>;

   registerCommands(registry: CommandRegistry): void {
      registry.registerCommand(SHOW_MODEL_COMMAND, { execute: () => this.showModel() });
   }

   protected async showModel(): Promise<void> {
      // The main area's, so focus in a side panel such as the Explorer still finds the editor.
      const widget = this.shell.getCurrentWidget('main');
      const uri = NavigatableWidget.is(widget) ? widget.getResourceUri() : undefined;
      if (
         uri === undefined ||
         !ALL_LANGUAGES.some(language => language.fileExtensions.some(extension => uri.path.base.endsWith(extension)))
      ) {
         this.messages.info(nls.localize('bookstore/showModel/noFile', 'Open a Bookstore file first.'));
         return;
      }
      this.session ??= this.connection.createSession('bookstore-show-model');
      const root = await this.session.withOpenDocument({ uri: uri.toString() }, document => document.model?.root.$type);
      this.messages.info(
         nls.localize(
            'bookstore/showModel/holds',
            '{0} holds a {1}',
            uri.path.base,
            root ?? nls.localize('bookstore/showModel/noModel', 'document with no model')
         )
      );
   }
}

import { injectable } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';

export class BookstoreGlspConnectionHandler extends GlspServerConnectionHandler {

      super({ languageContributionId: BOOKSTORE_GLSP_CONTRIBUTION_ID, portCommand: BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_HOST_COMMAND });
   }
}

theia/src/browser/bookstore-diagram-frontend-module.ts
==============================================================================
// The Bookstore diagram in Theia: the client package's diagram, opened from
// the language's files by a diagram manager. Its GLSP client is the one the
// extension's frontend module binds for every diagram.

import type { ContainerConfiguration } from '@eclipse-glsp/client';
import type { GLSPDiagramLanguage } from '@eclipse-glsp/theia-integration/lib/common';
import {
   AbstractHydraniumGlspDiagramConfiguration,
   AbstractHydraniumGlspDiagramManager,
   AbstractHydraniumGlspTheiaFrontendModule,
   createGlspClientTheiaModule,
   SkipClientContribution
} from '@hydranium/glsp-client-theia/browser';
import { type Container, ContainerModule, injectable } from '@theia/core/shared/inversify';
import { initializeBookstoreDiagramContainer } from 'bookstore-client';
import { BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_TYPE, BOOKSTORE_LANGUAGE } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { BOOKSTORE_GLSP_CONTRIBUTION_ID } from '../common/bookstore-glsp-contribution.js';
import '../../style/diagram.css';

export const BookstoreDiagramLanguage: GLSPDiagramLanguage = {
   contributionId: BOOKSTORE_GLSP_CONTRIBUTION_ID,
   label: 'Bookstore Diagram',
   diagramType: BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_TYPE,
   fileExtensions: [...BOOKSTORE_LANGUAGE.fileExtensions]
};

// Theia's host bindings, logging to the language client's Output channel. Passed
// after GLSP's Theia modules, whose bindings it replaces; a rebind made earlier
// is overwritten without an error.
const theiaModule = new ContainerModule((bind, unbind, isBound, rebind) => {
   createGlspClientTheiaModule({ bind, unbind, isBound, rebind }, { channelLogger: { channelName: 'Bookstore' } });
});

@injectable()
export class BookstoreDiagramConfiguration extends AbstractHydraniumGlspDiagramConfiguration {
   diagramType = BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_TYPE;
   // The LSP head already reports these problems.
   protected override propagateMarkersToProblemsView = false;

   configureContainer(container: Container, ...containerConfiguration: ContainerConfiguration): Container {
      return initializeBookstoreDiagramContainer(container, ...containerConfiguration, theiaModule);
   }
}

@injectable()
export class BookstoreDiagramManager extends AbstractHydraniumGlspDiagramManager {
   protected readonly diagramLanguage = BookstoreDiagramLanguage;
   protected readonly managerLabel = 'Bookstore Diagram Editor';

   override get id(): string {
      return 'bookstore-diagram-manager';
   }
}

export class BookstoreDiagramModule extends AbstractHydraniumGlspTheiaFrontendModule {
   readonly diagramLanguage = BookstoreDiagramLanguage;
   protected readonly diagramConfiguration = BookstoreDiagramConfiguration;
   protected readonly diagramManager = BookstoreDiagramManager;

   protected override bindClientContribution(): SkipClientContribution {
      return SkipClientContribution;
   }
}

export default new BookstoreDiagramModule();

theia/style/diagram.css

/* The diagrams' colours, from Theia's theme rather than GLSP's colours for a
   light canvas. Theia sizes the editor, so nothing here sets a height. */

.sprotty {
   background: var(--theia-editor-background);
   color: var(--theia-editor-foreground);
   font-family: var(--theia-ui-font-family);
   font-size: var(--theia-ui-font-size1);
}

/* GLSP's stylesheet leaves shapes at the SVG defaults: a black fill, and no stroke on an edge. */
.sprotty-node {
   fill: var(--theia-editorWidget-background);
   stroke: var(--theia-focusBorder);
}

.sprotty-edge {
   fill: none;
   stroke: var(--theia-editor-foreground);
}

==============================================================================
host-browser/README.md
==============================================================================
# bookstore-host-browser

Bookstore in a browser page: every head runs in a web worker, with no backend
and no Node runtime. The page saves through the LSP head, and the worker
keeps each saved file in IndexedDB, laid over `../workspace` on the next
load.

```bash
npm run build              # type-check and bundle into out/
npm start                  # serve the page at the URL it prints, rebundled on every source change
npm run test:e2e:install   # download the Chromium the smoke test drives, once
npm run test:e2e           # the smoke test, which serves the page itself
```

`PORT` moves the page to another port, for `npm start` and the smoke test alike;
stop `npm start` before the smoke test, or give one of them another port.
`npm start` reads `../workspace` once, so restart it after editing a file
there.

## Layout

- `index.html` — the page, with a pane for each head that stays hidden until its part fills it
- `hydranium-mark.svg` — the tab icon
- `esbuild.mjs` — bundles the page, the worker and Monaco’s worker, reading `../workspace` in as the seed
- `src/worker.ts` — the worker: the heads over one store, seeded and persisted
- `src/page.ts` — starts the worker and runs the part of the page each head serves
- `src/shown-file.ts` — the file switch above the panes, which every part follows
- `src/editor.ts` — the LSP part: a Monaco editor and Save
- `src/data-status.ts` — the data part: one document read through the data head
- `src/diagram.ts` — the GLSP part: the `Bookstore` diagram of the file the page shows, defined in the client package
- `src/log.ts` — the status line and the log area
- `src/workspace.ts` — the workspace root URI both ends name
- `src/monaco-editor-worker.ts` — Monaco’s own worker, which hosts no head
- `src/posix-path-shim.ts` — the `path` function the framework imports, for the bundle
- `test/smoke.spec.mts` — the page loads, each head answers, and a saved edit survives a reload

==============================================================================
host-browser/index.html
==============================================================================
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
   <head>
      <meta charset="utf-8" />
      <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
      <title>Bookstore</title>
      <!-- The stylesheets Monaco and GLSP import, which esbuild writes beside the page bundle. -->
      <link rel="stylesheet" href="./out/page.css" />
      <!-- The mark with white pages, which stays visible on a light and a dark tab strip alike. -->
      <link rel="icon" href="./hydranium-mark.svg" />
      <style>
         :root {
            --accent: #3b6ea8;
            --border: #dde1e6;
            --surface: #f6f7f9;
            --text: #1f2933;
            /* GLSP's marker colours, pure yellow and light blue by default, which a light page barely shows. */
            --glsp-error-foreground: #c62828;
            --glsp-warning-foreground: #b26a00;
            --glsp-info-foreground: var(--accent);
         }
         html,
         body {
            height: 100%;
            margin: 0;
         }
         body {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
            /* The window's width, which a long log line otherwise widens past it, cutting off the diagram. */
            grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
            font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
            font-size: 13px;
            color: var(--text);
         }
         /* The page's toolbar: its name, then the file switch, Save and the status they report to. */
         header {
            display: flex;
            gap: 12px;
            align-items: center;
            padding: 10px 16px;
            background: var(--accent);
            color: #ffffff;
         }
         h1 {
            margin: 0;
            font-size: 16px;
            font-weight: 600;
         }
         #status {
            padding: 2px 8px;
            border-radius: 10px;
            background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.18);
            font-size: 12px;
         }
         select,
         button {
            padding: 4px 10px;
            border: 1px solid var(--border);
            border-radius: 4px;
            background: #ffffff;
            color: var(--text);
            font: inherit;
         }
         /* On the toolbar's accent: white, with the accent as its text. */
         button {
            border-color: #ffffff;
            color: var(--accent);
            font-weight: 600;
            cursor: pointer;
         }
         button:hover {
            background: #e8eef6;
         }
         /* One column per shown pane, its title, hint and body rows shared, so the titles and hints line up. */
         main {
            display: grid;
            grid-auto-flow: column;
            grid-auto-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
            grid-template-rows: auto auto minmax(0, 1fr);
            min-height: 0;
         }
         main > section {
            display: grid;
            grid-row: 1 / -1;
            grid-template-rows: subgrid;
            min-width: 0;
            min-height: 0;
         }
         main > section[hidden] {
            display: none;
         }
         #diagram-pane {
            border-left: 1px solid var(--border);
         }
         .pane-title {
            margin: 0;
            padding: 10px 12px 2px;
            color: var(--accent);
            font-size: 12px;
            font-weight: 600;
            letter-spacing: 0.04em;
            text-transform: uppercase;
         }
         .hint {
            margin: 0;
            padding: 2px 12px 8px;
            border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border);
            color: #5f6b7a;
            font-size: 12px;
         }
         /* Shrinkable, or Monaco's width from before the diagram pane showed holds it at the whole window. */
         .pane-body {
            display: flex;
            flex-direction: column;
            min-width: 0;
            min-height: 0;
         }
         #editor {
            flex: 1 1 auto;
            min-height: 0;
         }
         /* The diagram needs a height, `position: relative` for its tool palette, and its `<svg>` sized to it. */
         #diagram {
            flex: 1 1 auto;
            position: relative;
            min-height: 0;
            background: var(--surface) radial-gradient(#d5dae1 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 16px 16px;
            touch-action: none;
         }
         /* GLSP's tool palette, in the page's colours. */
         .tool-palette {
            top: 12px;
            right: 44px;

==============================================================================
host-browser/esbuild.mjs
==============================================================================
// Bundles the page, the worker hosting the heads and, with an editor, Monaco's
// own worker into `out/`: once with `npm run build`, and on every change,
// served, with `npm start`.
//
// At `platform: 'browser'` esbuild refuses a `node:*` import rather than
// shimming it, so a Node import anywhere the worker reaches fails here rather
// than inside a worker with no console attached.

import { context } from 'esbuild';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url));
const workspace = fileURLToPath(new URL('../workspace/', import.meta.url));

// The worker's filesystem seed: each file of `../workspace`, keyed by its path
// below the workspace root. A file saved in the page is kept in IndexedDB and
// laid over this seed on the next load.
const seed = Object.fromEntries(
   readdirSync(workspace, { recursive: true, encoding: 'utf8' })
      .filter(path => statSync(join(workspace, path)).isFile())
      .map(path => [path.split('\\').join('/'), readFileSync(join(workspace, path), 'utf8')])
);

// Names the worker's IndexedDB database after this directory. Every project
// served on one port shares an origin, and with it the databases, so a name
// from the project alone lays one project's saved files over another's seed.
// Moving the directory starts again from the seed.
const directoryKey = createHash('sha256').update(root).digest('hex').slice(0, 12);

const common = {
   absWorkingDir: root,
   outdir: 'out',
   bundle: true,
   platform: 'browser',
   // Classic scripts: the page loads its bundle with a plain `<script>`, and
   // both workers are classic workers.
   format: 'iife',
   target: 'es2022',
   sourcemap: true,
   // The framework imports bare `path` so that a browser bundle can point it
   // at a shim. Relative to `absWorkingDir`.
   alias: { path: './src/posix-path-shim.ts' },
   define: {
      __WORKSPACE_SEED__: JSON.stringify(seed),
      __DIRECTORY_KEY__: JSON.stringify(directoryKey),
      __WORKER_BUNDLE_URL__: JSON.stringify('./out/worker.js'),
      __MONACO_WORKER_BUNDLE_URL__: JSON.stringify('./out/monaco-editor-worker.js')
   },
   logLevel: 'info'
};

// Monaco's own worker, on a page with an editor: `init` emits its source only
// with the LSP head.
const monacoEntry = 'src/monaco-editor-worker.ts';
const monacoWorker = existsSync(join(root, monacoEntry)) ? { 'monaco-editor-worker': monacoEntry } : {};

const builds = await Promise.all([
   context({
      ...common,
      entryPoints: { page: 'src/page.ts' },
      // The icon font Monaco and GLSP import, inlined: a `file` loader would
      // rewrite its URL relative to `out/`, which the page one directory up does
      // not resolve. The page's alone, so a diagram client import that reaches
      // the worker fails its bundle.
      loader: { '.ttf': 'dataurl' }
   }),
   context({ ...common, entryPoints: { worker: 'src/worker.ts', ...monacoWorker } })
]);

if (process.argv.includes('--serve')) {
   await Promise.all(builds.map(build => build.watch()));
   // On this machine only: the directory served holds the sources and `node_modules`.
   const requested = Number(process.env.PORT || 4937);
   const { port } = await builds[0].serve({ host: 'localhost', servedir: root, port: requested });
   console.log(`Serving http://localhost:${port}`);
} else {
   await Promise.all(builds.map(build => build.rebuild()));
   await Promise.all(builds.map(build => build.dispose()));
}

host-browser/playwright.config.mts

// The smoke tier: Playwright serves the page with `npm start` and drives it in
// Chromium, which `npm run test:e2e:install` downloads once. `npm start`
// bundles the page itself but not the packages it imports, so build those
// first.

import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';

/** The port `npm start` serves on; set `PORT` to run beside another server. */
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT || 4937);

export default defineConfig({
   testDir: './test',
   // The first load parses the grammar and builds the workspace in the worker.
   timeout: 60_000,
   expect: { timeout: 20_000 },
   use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], baseURL: `http://localhost:${PORT}` },
   webServer: {
      command: 'npm start',
      url: `http://localhost:${PORT}`,
      // A server already on the port fails the run rather than being tested in this one's place.
      reuseExistingServer: false,
      timeout: 120_000
   }
});

host-browser/src/worker.ts
==============================================================================
// The worker hosting the heads: every head over one store, in the browser and
// with no backend. The page reaches each head over a `MessagePort` of its own.

// First, before any class carrying a decorator loads: GLSP reads the metadata
// its decorators emit as each class is defined.
import 'reflect-metadata';
import { ServerModule } from '@eclipse-glsp/server/browser.js';
import { persistentFileSystem } from '@hydranium/core';
import { hostHeadsInWorker, IndexedDbFileSystemStore, startLanguageServerInWorker } from '@hydranium/core/browser';
import { DataServer } from '@hydranium/data-server';
import { startDataServerInWorker } from '@hydranium/data-server/browser';
import { GlspClientLogger, HydraniumGlspAppModule } from '@hydranium/glsp-server';
import { startGlspServerInWorker } from '@hydranium/glsp-server/browser';
import type { BookstoreModel } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { BookstoreDiagramModule, createBookstoreServices } from 'bookstore-server';
import { WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI } from './workspace.js';

/** The files of `../workspace`, read by `esbuild.mjs` and keyed by their path below the root. */
declare const __WORKSPACE_SEED__: Record<string, string>;
/** This project's directory, hashed by `esbuild.mjs`, so that no other project on the origin opens its store. */
declare const __DIRECTORY_KEY__: string;

// A saved file is kept in IndexedDB and laid over the seed on the next load;
// the heads start once the stored files are restored.
const store = new IndexedDbFileSystemStore(`bookstore-workspace-${__DIRECTORY_KEY__}`);

hostHeadsInWorker(
   persistentFileSystem({ store, seed: __WORKSPACE_SEED__, rootUri: WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI }),
   (ports, fileSystem) => {
      // The LSP head composes the services, as the Node entry does around stdio.
      const shared = startLanguageServerInWorker(ports.lsp, connection => createBookstoreServices({ connection, ...fileSystem }).shared);
      // The data head serves from the LSP head's store, on its own port.
      startDataServerInWorker(ports.data, shared, connection => new DataServer<BookstoreModel>(connection, shared));
      const glsp = startGlspServerInWorker({
         context: ports.glsp,
         createLogger: caller => new GlspClientLogger(shared, { component: caller }),
         serverModule: new ServerModule().configureDiagramModule(new BookstoreDiagramModule()),
         appModules: [new HydraniumGlspAppModule({ shared })]
      });
      // The GLSP head reports a failed start through `started`, which the
      // ready message waits for.
      return { shared, started: [glsp.started] };
   },
   // The ready message then carries the workspace files the page opens.
   { rootUri: WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI }
);

==============================================================================
host-browser/src/page.ts
==============================================================================
// The page: it starts the worker, hands each head a channel of its own, and
// fills the pane of each head the server runs, one after the other.

import { connectWorkerHeads } from '@hydranium/client-browser';
import { ConsoleLogger, describeError } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import { ALL_LANGUAGES } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { showDataStatus } from './data-status.js';
import { mountDiagram, settleDiagramEdits } from './diagram.js';
import { armEditorSave, startEditor } from './editor.js';
import { appendLog, setStatus } from './log.js';
import { startShownFile } from './shown-file.js';
import { WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI } from './workspace.js';

/** Where the worker bundle is served, substituted by `esbuild.mjs`. */
declare const __WORKER_BUNDLE_URL__: string;

async function main(): Promise<void> {
   // The page's end of each head's connection logs to the browser console.
   const logger = new ConsoleLogger();
   const heads = connectWorkerHeads(new Worker(__WORKER_BUNDLE_URL__), { logger });
   heads.onWorkerError(report => appendLog(`worker error during ${report.phase}: ${report.message}`));
   setStatus('starting…');
   const shownFile = await startShownFile(heads, ALL_LANGUAGES);
   const editor = await startEditor(heads, shownFile);
   let shownDiagram: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof mountDiagram>> | undefined = undefined;
   armEditorSave(editor, () => settleDiagramEdits(shownDiagram?.()));
   await showDataStatus(heads.data, `${WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI}/nodes.bookstore`);
   shownDiagram = await mountDiagram(heads.glsp, shownFile, logger, settleDiagramEdits);
   setStatus('ready');
}

main().catch((error: unknown) => setStatus(`failed: ${describeError(error)}`));

==============================================================================
host-browser/src/shown-file.ts
==============================================================================
// The file the page shows: the switch above the panes, between the workspace
// files the worker holds. Each part follows it, and any part can switch it, so
// a page with one part fewer still has it.

import type { WorkerHeads } from '@hydranium/client-browser';
import { WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI } from './workspace.js';

/** The file the page shows, for each part that follows it. */
export interface ShownFile {
   /** Each workspace file a language claims, by URI, with the text the worker holds. */
   readonly files: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
   /** The URI of the file shown now. */
   current(): string;
   /** Switch the page to `uri`, one of {@link files}. */
   show(uri: string): void;
   /** Call `listener` with the URI of each file the page switches to. */
   onDidChange(listener: (uri: string) => void): void;
}

/**
 * Fill the switch with the files of `languages` the worker sent once its heads
 * were up, and show the first.
 */
export async function startShownFile(
   heads: WorkerHeads,
   languages: ReadonlyArray<{ readonly fileExtensions: readonly string[] }>
): Promise<ShownFile> {
   // The text comes from the worker rather than the seed, since a saved edit
   // is laid over the seed there.
   const { workspace } = await heads.ready;
   if (workspace === undefined) {
      throw new Error('the worker sent no workspace files');
   }
   // Only the files a part of the page can show: one of another language would show nothing.
   const claimed = (path: string): boolean =>
      languages.some(language => language.fileExtensions.some(extension => path.endsWith(extension)));
   const paths = Object.keys(workspace.files).filter(claimed).sort();
   if (paths.length === 0) {
      throw new Error('no workspace file has an extension the page shows');
   }
   const files = new Map(paths.map(path => [`${WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI}/${path}`, workspace.files[path]]));

   const select = document.getElementById('file') as HTMLSelectElement;
   // The worker keys each file by its encoded path, as in its URI: shown decoded.
   select.append(...paths.map(path => new Option(decodeURIComponent(path), `${WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI}/${path}`)));
   let shown = select.value;
   const listeners: Array<(uri: string) => void> = [];
   const show = (uri: string): void => {
      if (!files.has(uri)) {
         throw new Error(`${uri} is not a workspace file the page shows`);
      }
      select.value = uri;
      if (uri !== shown) {
         shown = uri;
         listeners.forEach(listener => listener(uri));
      }
   };
   select.addEventListener('change', () => show(select.value));
   select.hidden = false;
   return { files, current: () => shown, show, onDidChange: listener => listeners.push(listener) };
}

==============================================================================
host-browser/src/editor.ts
==============================================================================
// The LSP part of the page: one Monaco editor over the LSP head, showing the
// file the page shows, and Save. The worker holds the files, so the page saves
// through the LSP head and the worker writes them to IndexedDB.

import { initializeLanguageClient, type WorkerHeads } from '@hydranium/client-browser';
import { MONACO_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES, MonacoLspClient } from '@hydranium/client-browser/monaco';
import { describeError } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import { ALL_LANGUAGES } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { PublishDiagnosticsNotification } from 'vscode-languageserver-protocol';
import { appendLog, setStatus } from './log.js';
import type { ShownFile } from './shown-file.js';
import { WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI } from './workspace.js';

/** Where Monaco's own worker bundle is served, substituted by `esbuild.mjs`. */
declare const __MONACO_WORKER_BUNDLE_URL__: string;

// Before any editor exists: Monaco otherwise looks for a worker script no
// bundle emits, and fails on the first edit.
self.MonacoEnvironment = { getWorker: () => new Worker(__MONACO_WORKER_BUNDLE_URL__) };

/** Each language as Monaco registers it, from the ids and extensions the server generates. */
const LANGUAGES = ALL_LANGUAGES.map(language => ({
   id: language.languageId,
   extensions: [...language.fileExtensions]
}));

/**
 * Run the LSP handshake, then show the page's shown file in the editor,
 * following each switch, and hand back the client {@link armEditorSave} saves
 * through.
 */
export async function startEditor(heads: WorkerHeads, shownFile: ShownFile): Promise<MonacoLspClient> {
   let client!: MonacoLspClient;
   await initializeLanguageClient(heads.lsp, {
      rootUri: WORKSPACE_ROOT_URI,
      capabilities: MONACO_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES,
      onLogMessage: params => appendLog(params.message),
      // Before `initialized`, since the server publishes from then on.
      beforeInitialized: result => {
         client = new MonacoLspClient(heads.lsp, result.capabilities, { languages: LANGUAGES });
         heads.lsp.onNotification(PublishDiagnosticsNotification.type, params => client.applyDiagnostics(params));
      }
   });

   const modelOf = (uri: string) => client.openDocument(uri, shownFile.files.get(uri) as string);
   const editor = client.createEditor(document.getElementById('editor') as HTMLElement, modelOf(shownFile.current()), {
      automaticLayout: true,
      minimap: { enabled: false },
      scrollBeyondLastLine: false,
      wordWrap: 'on'
   });
   shownFile.onDidChange(uri => editor.setModel(modelOf(uri)));

   // Go to definition across files switches the editor to the target file.
   client.registerEditorOpener((uri, position) => {
      if (!shownFile.files.has(uri)) {
         return false;
      }
      shownFile.show(uri);
      editor.setPosition(position);
      editor.revealPositionInCenter(position);
      return true;
   });

   // Asks before a reload or a closed tab drops an unsaved edit.
   window.addEventListener('beforeunload', event => {
      if (client.dirtyDocuments().length > 0) {
         event.preventDefault();
      }
   });
   (document.getElementById('editor-pane') as HTMLElement).hidden = false;
   return client;
}

/**
 * Arm the page's Save and Ctrl+S, which save every file the editor holds
 * unsaved once `beforeSave` has settled: an edit made elsewhere, such as in the
 * diagram, shows in the editor only once the server has answered it. When
 * `beforeSave` throws, nothing is saved and the status says why.
 */
export function armEditorSave(client: MonacoLspClient, beforeSave: () => Promise<void> = () => Promise.resolve()): void {
   const save = (): void => {
      // The wait can last up to its bound on a server that stopped answering.
      setStatus('saving…');
      beforeSave()
         .then(() => client.saveAll())
         .then(
            saved => setStatus(`saved ${saved.length} file(s)`),
            (error: unknown) => setStatus(`save failed: ${describeError(error)}`)
         );
   };
   const saveButton = document.getElementById('save') as HTMLButtonElement;
   saveButton.addEventListener('click', save);
   // Ctrl+S (Cmd+S) saves too, in place of the browser's "Save page as".
   window.addEventListener('keydown', event => {
      if ((event.ctrlKey || event.metaKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === 's') {
         event.preventDefault();
         save();
      }
   });
   saveButton.hidden = false;
}

==============================================================================
host-browser/src/data-status.ts
==============================================================================
// The data part of the page: one document read through the data head, out of
// the same store the other heads serve.

import { DataConnectionWithEvents, type DataPort } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import type { BookstoreElement } from 'bookstore-protocol';

/** Open `uri` through the data head and say what it holds on the status line below the panes. */
export async function showDataStatus(port: DataPort, uri: string): Promise<void> {
   const session = new DataConnectionWithEvents<BookstoreElement>(port).createSession('bookstore-page');
   const opened = await session.openDocument({ uri });
   const line = document.getElementById('data-status') as HTMLElement;
   const file = uri.slice(uri.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
   line.textContent = `data head: ${file} holds a ${opened.model?.root.$type ?? 'document with no model'}`;
   line.hidden = false;
}

==============================================================================
host-browser/src/diagram.ts
==============================================================================
// The GLSP part of the page: the Bookstore diagram of the file the page
// shows, drawn by the client module every host of this project mounts.

import type { WorkerHeads } from '@hydranium/client-browser';
import { glspConnection, type GlspDiagramMount, HydraniumGlspClient, mountGlspDiagram } from '@hydranium/glsp-client';
import { describeError, type Logger } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import { initializeBookstoreDiagramContainer } from 'bookstore-client';
import { BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_TYPE, BOOKSTORE_LANGUAGE } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { appendLog } from './log.js';
import type { ShownFile } from './shown-file.js';

/**
 * Show the diagram of the file the page shows, and of each file it switches
 * to, and hand back what reads the mount shown now, if it loaded. A file of
 * another language hides the pane. `beforeLeave` runs on the shown mount
 * before a switch disposes it, while the diagram takes no input; when it
 * throws, that mount stays shown and the page switches back to its file.
 */
export async function mountDiagram(
   connection: WorkerHeads['glsp'],
   shownFile: ShownFile,
   logger: Logger,
   beforeLeave?: (mount: GlspDiagramMount) => Promise<void>
): Promise<() => GlspDiagramMount | undefined> {
   const glspClient = new HydraniumGlspClient({ id: 'diagram', connectionProvider: glspConnection(connection) });
   let mounted: GlspDiagramMount | undefined;
   let mountedUri: string | undefined;
   const show = async (uri: string): Promise<void> => {
      // Switched away while queued: the show queued for the newer file replaces this one.
      // Switched back before the switch away ran: its diagram is still the one shown.
      if (uri !== shownFile.current() || uri === mountedUri) {
         return;
      }
      // Only a mount that loaded: one that failed has no edits to lose, and its
      // dispatcher may refuse every save, which would keep it shown for good.
      if (mounted !== undefined && mountedUri !== undefined && beforeLeave !== undefined) {
         // Inert, since an edit made while it runs would outlast its wait and be dropped with the mount.
         const shown = document.getElementById('diagram') as HTMLElement;
         shown.inert = true;
         try {
            await beforeLeave(mounted);
         } catch (error: unknown) {
            // The diagram stays on its file, so the switch goes back to it.
            shownFile.show(mountedUri);
            throw error;
         } finally {
            shown.inert = false;
         }
         // Switched again while it ran: the show queued for that file takes over.
         if (uri !== shownFile.current()) {
            return;
         }
      }
      mounted?.dispose();
      mounted = undefined;
      mountedUri = undefined;
      // A fresh element, since a disposed mount leaves what it drew.
      const element = document.createElement('div');
      element.id = 'diagram';
      (document.getElementById('diagram') as HTMLElement).replaceWith(element);
      const pane = document.getElementById('diagram-pane') as HTMLElement;
      // Shown before the mount, which measures the element it draws into.
      pane.hidden = !BOOKSTORE_LANGUAGE.fileExtensions.some(extension => uri.endsWith(extension));
      if (pane.hidden) {
         return;
      }
      mounted = await mountGlspDiagram({
         mount: element,
         diagramType: BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_TYPE,
         sourceUri: uri,
         glspClient,
         initializeDiagramContainer: initializeBookstoreDiagramContainer,
         logger
      });
      if (mounted.loadOutcome.status === 'failed') {
         throw new Error(`the diagram of ${uri} did not load: ${describeError(mounted.loadOutcome.error)}`);
      }
      mountedUri = uri;
   };

   // One mount at a time, so one still loading is not disposed half built, and a
   // failed one does not stop the next.
   let switching: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
   const follow = (uri: string): Promise<void> => {
      const shown = switching.then(() => show(uri));
      switching = shown.catch(() => undefined);
      return shown;
   };
   // Before the first mount, since the page can switch while it loads.
   shownFile.onDidChange(uri => {
      follow(uri).catch((error: unknown) => appendLog(describeError(error)));
   });
   // A first file that fails to load is logged as a later switch's is, so the
   // page still arms what follows and the switch can reach a file that loads.
   await follow(shownFile.current()).catch((error: unknown) => appendLog(describeError(error)));
   // Asks before a reload or a closed tab drops an edit the server has not
   // answered yet, which neither dirty state nor the editor shows until then.
   window.addEventListener('beforeunload', event => {
      if ((mounted?.editsInFlight ?? 0) > 0) {
         event.preventDefault();
      }
   });
   // Only a mount that loaded: one that failed has nothing to save.
   return () => (mountedUri === undefined ? undefined : mounted);
}

/**
 * Wait for the edits of `diagram` the server has not answered yet, before a
 * save, which would miss them, or before a switch disposes it, as the server
 * drops what an ended session still had queued and the reload guard reads only
 * the diagram shown. Throws when one stays unanswered, so the save does not
 * report success and the switch keeps the diagram shown.
 */
export async function settleDiagramEdits(diagram: GlspDiagramMount | undefined): Promise<void> {
   if ((await diagram?.whenEditsSettled()) === false) {
      throw new Error('the server has not answered an edit of this diagram yet');
   }
}

// The page's status line and log area: what the page is told and the errors
// it reports.

/** Replace the one-line status in the title bar. */
export function setStatus(text: string): void {
   (document.getElementById('status') as HTMLElement).textContent = text;
}

/** Add a line to the log area, kept scrolled to its end. */
export function appendLog(text: string): void {
   const log = document.getElementById('log') as HTMLElement;
   log.append(`${text}\n`);
   log.scrollTop = log.scrollHeight;
}

==============================================================================
host-browser/src/posix-path-shim.ts
==============================================================================
// The one function of Node's `path` the framework imports, for the bundle to
// resolve: `esbuild.mjs` points the bare `path` specifier here, while a
// `node:path` import still fails the bundle. Only a workspace folder given as
// a filesystem path reaches it, which the page, naming a URI, never does.

/** Resolve `segments` right to left into one absolute path, as `path.posix.resolve` does from `/`. */
export function resolve(...segments: string[]): string {
   let resolved = '';
   for (let i = segments.length - 1; i >= 0 && !resolved.startsWith('/'); i--) {
      if (segments[i].length > 0) {
         resolved = resolved.length === 0 ? segments[i] : `${segments[i]}/${resolved}`;
      }
   }
   const parts: string[] = [];
   for (const part of resolved.split('/')) {
      if (part === '..') {
         parts.pop();
      } else if (part !== '' && part !== '.') {
         parts.push(part);
      }
   }
   return `/${parts.join('/')}`;
}

==============================================================================
host-browser/test/smoke.spec.mts
==============================================================================
// The page loads with every head answering, and an edit saved through the
// LSP head is still there after a reload; any console error fails that
// test. The other asks before a reload drops a diagram edit the server has not
// answered yet, and keeps it when Save is clicked at once.

import { expect, test } from '@playwright/test';

test('loads every head and keeps a saved edit across a reload', async ({ page }) => {
   const errors: string[] = [];
   page.on('pageerror', error => errors.push(error.message));
   page.on('console', message => {
      if (message.type() === 'error') {
         errors.push(message.text());
      }
   });
   const editor = page.locator('#editor .view-lines');

   await page.goto('/');
   await expect(page.locator('#status')).toHaveText('ready');
   await expect(editor).toContainText('node First');
   // The data head reads the document out of the same store.
   await expect(page.locator('#data-status')).toHaveText('data head: nodes.bookstore holds a BookstoreModel');
   // The diagram follows the switch: two nodes in one file, and in the other its
   // node and the target it references there, drawn as external.
   const first = await page.locator('#file').inputValue();
   await page.locator('#file').selectOption('nodes.bookstore');
   await expect(page.locator('#diagram .sprotty-node')).toHaveCount(2);
   await page.locator('#file').selectOption('references.bookstore');
   await expect(page.locator('#diagram .external')).toHaveText('Second (nodes.bookstore)');
   await page.locator('#file').selectOption(first);

   await editor.click();
   await page.keyboard.press('ControlOrMeta+End');
   await page.keyboard.type('\nnode Added');
   await page.locator('#save').click();
   await expect(page.locator('#status')).toHaveText('saved 1 file(s)');

   await page.reload();
   await expect(page.locator('#status')).toHaveText('ready');
   await expect(editor).toContainText('node Added');
   expect(errors).toEqual([]);
});

test('asks before a reload drops a diagram edit the server has not answered, and saves it with Save at once', async ({ page }) => {
   const nodes = page.locator('#diagram .sprotty-node');
   const askGuard = (): Promise<boolean> =>
      page.evaluate(() => {
         const event = new Event('beforeunload', { cancelable: true });
         window.dispatchEvent(event);
         return event.defaultPrevented;
      });
   await page.goto('/');
   await expect(page.locator('#status')).toHaveText('ready');
   await page.locator('#file').selectOption('nodes.bookstore');
   await expect(nodes).toHaveCount(2);

   const canvas = page.locator('#diagram');
   await page.locator('#diagram .tool-button', { hasText: 'BookstoreNode' }).click();
   const size = await canvas.evaluate(element => ({ width: element.clientWidth, height: element.clientHeight }));
   // Asked and clicked right after the click's own handlers, in the same turn
   // of the page, so the server's answer cannot have marked anything unsaved.
   await page.evaluate(() => {
      window.addEventListener(
         'mouseup',
         () =>
            queueMicrotask(() => {
               const event = new Event('beforeunload', { cancelable: true });
               window.dispatchEvent(event);
               document.getElementById('save')?.click();
               Reflect.set(window, 'guardedOnCreate', event.defaultPrevented);
            }),
         { once: true }
      );
   });
   await canvas.click({ position: { x: size.width * 0.4, y: size.height * 0.85 } });
   expect(await page.evaluate(() => Reflect.get(window, 'guardedOnCreate'))).toBe(true);
   await expect(page.locator('#status')).toHaveText('saved 1 file(s)');
   expect(await askGuard()).toBe(false);

   await page.reload();
   await expect(page.locator('#status')).toHaveText('ready');
   await page.locator('#file').selectOption('nodes.bookstore');
   await expect(nodes).toHaveCount(3);
});

==============================================================================
host-vscode/README.md
==============================================================================
# bookstore-host-vscode

Bookstore in VS Code: the language client, and a custom editor drawing each
diagram file. The server is started by `../vscode-servers`, whose launch this
extension calls, so the two never hand the server different documents. It needs
a Node extension host: the server is forked, and its socket heads are reached
over TCP.

`Bookstore: Show Model`, in the Command Palette, reads the active file through
the data head over a socket from the extension host, and names its root type. A
webview reaches the data head too: see the Host in VS Code guide.

```bash
npm run build              # copy the server’s grammars, type-check and compile, then bundle
npm run watch              # copy the grammars and recompile and rebundle on every change; Developer: Reload Window picks it up
npm start                  # VS Code with this extension, on ../workspace; needs `code` on the PATH
npm run test:e2e:install   # download the VS Code the smoke test drives, once
npm run test:e2e           # the smoke test; under `xvfb-run -a` on Linux without a display
```

## Layout

- `src/extension.ts` — activation: the server, through `../vscode-servers`, the Show Model command, and the diagram editors
- `src/show-model-command.ts` — Show Model: the active file, read through the data head
- `src/bookstore-diagram-editor.ts` — the `Bookstore` diagram’s custom editor; its view type is the one `package.json` declares
- `src/webview/bookstore-diagram.ts` — the webview it loads, over the client package’s diagram
- `src/webview/diagram.css` — the webview’s size and colours
- `esbuild.mjs` — bundles each webview into `out/webview/`
- `start.mjs` — `npm start`: VS Code with this extension, on `../workspace`
- `test/smoke.spec.mts` — VS Code opens the workspace, Show Model names the model, the diagram draws, and the server reports a broken reference
- `test/vscode-version.mts` — the VS Code release the smoke test runs

// without a display, run it under `xvfb-run -a`.

import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
   testDir: './test',
   // The first request waits for the server to build the workspace.

   expect: { timeout: 60_000 },

==============================================================================
host-vscode/start.mjs
==============================================================================
// Starts VS Code with this extension on `../workspace`. VS Code reads a
// relative `--extensionDevelopmentPath` against its own working directory
// rather than this one, so both paths are made absolute here.

import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const args = [
   `--extensionDevelopmentPath=${fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url))}`,
   fileURLToPath(new URL('../workspace', import.meta.url))
];
// On Windows `code` is a `.cmd`, which only a shell runs. The shell gets one
// command line, as Node deprecates arguments beside `shell: true`, and each
// path is quoted so the shell does not split one with a space.
const child =
   process.platform === 'win32'
      ? spawn(['code', ...args.map(arg => `"${arg}"`)].join(' '), { stdio: 'inherit', shell: true })
      : spawn('code', args, { stdio: 'inherit' });
child.on('error', error => {
   console.error(`Could not start VS Code: ${error.message}. npm start needs \`code\` on the PATH.`);
   process.exitCode = 1;
});

==============================================================================
host-vscode/src/extension.ts
==============================================================================
// The Bookstore VS Code extension: the language client, started the way the
// servers extension starts it, a Show Model command reading a file through the
// data head, and a custom editor for each diagram. Node extension host only:
// the server is forked and its socket heads reached over TCP.

import { findPort } from '@hydranium/client-vscode/node';
import { SocketDataPort } from '@hydranium/data-client-vscode/node';
import { HydraniumGlspVscodeConnector, HydraniumGlspVscodeServer } from '@hydranium/glsp-client-vscode/node';
import { ConsoleLogger, DataConnectionWithEvents, describeError, renderFrameworkMessage } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import { BOOKSTORE_DATA_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND, BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND, type BookstoreElement } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { commands, type ExtensionContext, window } from 'vscode';
import type { LanguageClient } from 'vscode-languageclient/node';
import { startBookstoreLanguageClient } from 'bookstore-vscode-servers/out/language-client.js';
import { BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_VIEW_TYPE, BookstoreDiagramEditorProvider } from './bookstore-diagram-editor.js';
import { showModelCommand } from './show-model-command.js';

let client: LanguageClient | undefined;

export async function activate(context: ExtensionContext): Promise<void> {
   const running = await startBookstoreLanguageClient(context);
   client = running;

   // The data head, read by the Show Model command. Nothing connects until it runs.
   const dataPort = new SocketDataPort({
      findPort: () => findPort(running, BOOKSTORE_DATA_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND),
      logger: new ConsoleLogger().with('data head'),
      // A failed read shown to the user, not only logged; the message carries the detail.
      reportError: (_error, reported) => void window.showErrorMessage(renderFrameworkMessage(reported))
   });
   const dataConnection = new DataConnectionWithEvents<BookstoreElement>(dataPort);
   context.subscriptions.push(dataConnection, dataPort, commands.registerCommand('bookstore.showModel', showModelCommand(dataConnection)));

   // The GLSP head, and the connector bridging it to every diagram webview. No
   // `messenger` option: the connector's own keeps messages flowing to a hidden tab.
   const glspServer = new HydraniumGlspVscodeServer({
      clientId: 'bookstore-glsp',
      clientName: 'Bookstore',
      findPort: () => findPort(running, BOOKSTORE_GLSP_SERVER_PORT_COMMAND),
      logger: new ConsoleLogger().with('GLSP head')
   });
   const glspConnector = new HydraniumGlspVscodeConnector({ server: glspServer, logging: false });
   context.subscriptions.push(glspServer, glspConnector);
   // Not awaited, so a session that opens no diagram does not wait on the port.
   // `start()` resolves either way; a failure is reported off `onReady`.
   void glspServer.start();
   void glspServer.onReady.catch((error: unknown) => {
      void window.showErrorMessage(`Bookstore diagram unavailable: ${describeError(error)}`);
   });
   const bookstoreEditor = new BookstoreDiagramEditorProvider(glspConnector, context.extensionUri);
   context.subscriptions.push(
      window.registerCustomEditorProvider(BOOKSTORE_DIAGRAM_VIEW_TYPE, bookstoreEditor, {
         // A hidden tab keeps its diagram session rather than repeating the handshake.
         webviewOptions: { retainContextWhenHidden: true },
         // Two views of one document would be two GLSP clients racing on one model.
         supportsMultipleEditorsPerDocument: false
      })
   );
}

export async function deactivate(): Promise<void> {
   await client?.stop();
   client = undefined;
}

==============================================================================
host-vscode/src/show-model-command.ts
==============================================================================
// `Bookstore: Show Model`: the active tab's file, text or diagram, read through
// the data head, and its root type shown in a notification.

import type { DataConnectionWithEvents } from '@hydranium/protocol';
import { ALL_LANGUAGES, type BookstoreElement } from 'bookstore-protocol';
import { TabInputCustom, TabInputText, window } from 'vscode';

/** The command's handler, reading through `connection`. */
export function showModelCommand(connection: DataConnectionWithEvents<BookstoreElement>): () => Promise<void> {
   // Opened on the first run and kept until the connection is disposed.
   let session: ReturnType<typeof connection.createSession> | undefined;
   return async () => {
      const input = window.tabGroups.activeTabGroup.activeTab?.input;
      const uri = input instanceof TabInputText || input instanceof TabInputCustom ? input.uri : undefined;
      if (uri === undefined || !ALL_LANGUAGES.some(language => language.fileExtensions.some(extension => uri.path.endsWith(extension)))) {
         void window.showInformationMessage('Open a Bookstore file first.');
         return;
      }
      session ??= connection.createSession('bookstore-show-model');
      const root = await session.withOpenDocument({ uri: uri.toString() }, document => document.model?.root.$type);
      const file = uri.path.slice(uri.path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1);
      void window.showInformationMessage(`${file} holds a ${root ?? 'document with no model'}`);
   };
}

// The diagram webviews' half: a browser page, so it has the DOM. esbuild
// emits, so this only type-checks, and the stylesheet imports are esbuild's to
// resolve.
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM"],
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "noUncheckedSideEffectImports": false,
    "types": []
  },
  "include": ["src/webview"]
